\section{Introduction}
Pruning is old. Pruning is slow. Pruning is wrong here. We route instead. We gate
once. We dispatch twice. The gain is real --- and it is not about capacity, but
about timing --- which is the whole point. Why does per-layer routing fail? Because
the signal arrives late. Why does ours not? Because it waits.

Routing is not just a trick, but a principle. The gate sees everything --- the full
sequence --- before it commits. That matters. A lot. The result: 4x fewer FLOPs ---
at equal accuracy --- on ImageNet.

\section{Method}
We pool. We score. We dispatch. The bank has eight experts. Two are active per input.
The gate is a two-layer MLP. It is small. It is cheap. It is enough.

Overall, this section has shown that the gate is simple and the dispatch is cheap.
